title: History at a Glance – Part 1
text:
Below you find checked knowledge.

The first Moon landing was in 1969 with Apollo 11. So much for that. World War II lasted from 1939 to 1945. This matters too. World War I lasted from 1914 to 1918. Moving on. The Berlin Wall was the fortified border between East and West Berlin from 1961 to 1989.

So much for that. The Berlin Wall fell on 9 November 1989. Let's continue with the next point. The telephone was patented by Alexander Graham Bell in 1876, with key pioneer work by Antonio Meucci. This matters too. Relativity theory was developed by Albert Einstein. This matters too.

Democracy means rule by the people, usually through free elections and basic rights. Moving on. The EU is a union of European states with a single market and shared institutions. So much for that. The EU has 27 member states. One more fact. The Basic Law is the constitution of Germany, in force since 1949.

Let's continue with the next point. Germany was reunified in 1990. So much for that. The Middle Ages was the era from about 500 to 1500, between antiquity and modern times. Continuing. Leonardo da Vinci was an Italian artist and inventor, famous for the Mona Lisa. Let's continue with the next point.

Marie Curie was a physicist who researched radioactivity and won two Nobel prizes.

Now you know the facts.

title: History at a Glance – Part 2
text:
Here you learn ordered knowledge. Take your time.

The French Revolution from 1789 overthrew the monarchy under liberty, equality, fraternity. This matters too. Human rights are basic rights of every person, such as life, liberty and equality. Let's continue with the next point. Inflation means prices rise and money loses value. Let's continue with the next point. Industrialization was the shift to machines and factories starting in the 18th century.

So much for that. The basics date to ARPANET in 1969, the World Wide Web from 1989. One more fact. The car was invented by Carl Benz with the 1886 motor car. Moving on. The first powered flight was made by the Wright brothers in 1903. One more fact.

For the Bundestag from age 18. In European elections in Germany from 16. So much for that. Eligible voters cast ballots, votes are counted and seats assigned by result. One more fact. In a dictatorship one person or group rules without free elections; in a democracy power comes from the people. So much for that. Sustainability means living so future generations also have enough resources.

Moving on. Bullying is repeated harassment or exclusion. Talk to trusted people, document incidents, get help. Continuing. Peace means living together without war and violence. Continuing. Freedom means living self-determined without harming others. Continuing.

Justice means fair and equal treatment for everyone.

That was the most important part.

title: Nature, Science and Technology – Part 1
text:
Below you find checked knowledge.

The sky is blue due to Rayleigh scattering: blue sunlight is scattered more in the atmosphere than red. Moving on. Rain forms by evaporation: water rises, cools, forms clouds and falls back as drops. This matters too. Photosynthesis is how plants make sugar and oxygen from light, water and CO2. Moving on. Weather is the short-term state of the atmosphere; climate is the average over about 30 years.

Continuing. A fridge pumps heat from inside out with coolant: it evaporates inside, absorbs heat, releases it outside. This matters too. Electricity is simply the directed movement of electric charges, usually electrons in a wire. This matters too. Water is H2O, a compound of hydrogen and oxygen. This matters too.

A virus is a tiny pathogen that cannot multiply without a host cell. One more fact. Artificial intelligence means programs that learn from data, recognize patterns and solve tasks like text or images. So much for that. A browser is the program you open websites with, e.g. Chrome, Firefox, Edge or Safari. Continuing. An app is an application program, usually for phones, e.g. for messages, photos or games.

So much for that. Water keeps circulation and focus stable, helps kidneys and skin, prevents headaches. One more fact. About 2 minutes, twice a day. Moving on. Gravity is the attraction between masses. Earth pulls everything down, so things fall. Let's continue with the next point.

Air is a gas mix, mostly nitrogen and oxygen.

This ends the overview.

title: Nature, Science and Technology – Part 2
text:
This text presents important facts. Read it calmly.

The heart pumps blood through the body. Moving on. The lungs take up oxygen and release carbon dioxide. So much for that. Sleep supports recovery, memory and the immune system. Continuing. Fever is raised body temperature, often a defense against infection.

One more fact. A strong password is long, unique per service and best stored in a password manager. Let's continue with the next point. Wi-Fi is a wireless local network for internet without cables. One more fact. The cloud means servers on the internet where you store data and use services. So much for that.

GPS finds position from signals of several satellites and their travel time. This matters too. Day and night exist because Earth rotates. The sunny side has day, the other night. Continuing. Seasons come from the tilt of Earth axis: each hemisphere leans toward the sun in turn. This matters too. The Moon shines because it reflects sunlight.

This matters too. The Sun is a star of hot gas giving light and warmth. One more fact. Our solar system has 8 planets: Mercury, Venus, Earth, Mars, Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus, Neptune. Continuing. An atom is the smallest unit of matter, made of nucleus and electrons. Let's continue with the next point.

Recycling means collecting waste and turning it into new products.

This ends the overview.

title: Nature, Science and Technology – Part 3
text:
This text explains facts step by step.

The greenhouse effect traps heat in the atmosphere. Too many greenhouse gases warm the climate further. Let's continue with the next point. Bees pollinate plants, securing harvests and biodiversity. Moving on. Leaves are green because of chlorophyll, the pigment for photosynthesis. One more fact. Mammals have fur, give birth to live young and nurse them with milk.

Let's continue with the next point. A battery turns chemical energy into electric energy. Continuing. Solar cells turn sunlight directly into electric power. Continuing. A computer virus is a harmful program that spreads and causes damage. Protect with updates and care with attachments. So much for that.

Plastic barely rots, litters nature and seas, and breaks into microplastics. So much for that. An earthquake happens when tectonic plates move suddenly and release energy. Continuing. Honey is made by bees from flower nectar.

Now you know the facts.

text:

Download offline maps, follow signs, ask locals.
